dataset.name: Yakima River Basin Temporal Study: Sensor and Sample Data from Wenas Creek following the Evans Canyon Fire in Washington, USA
description: The Evans Canyon Fire occurred in Washington in August 2020 and burned 76,000 acres of the semi-arid shrub-steppe landscape at low to moderate severities. This fire burned across the Wenas Creek watershed, allowing for a sampling design that included a portion of the stream within the burned area and a reference site upstream of the burn. Monthly data was collected at an unburned (W10) and burned (W20) site from November 2020 to August 2022 for in situ hydrological and water chemistry sensor data, handheld sensor water chemistry data, general environmental context photos, and field metadata.

This dataset is comprised of one folder with field photos and one main data folder containing (1) sensor and sample field protocols; (2) file-level metadata (flmd); (3) data dictionary (dd); (4) international geo-sample number (IGSN) mapping file; (5) field metadata; (6) readme; (7) methods codes; (8) dissolved organic carbon (DOC; measured as non-purgeable organic carbon; NPOC); (9) total nitrogen (TN); (10) total suspended solids (TSS); (11) sensor data (specific conductance, pH, total dissolved solids, temperature, pressure, dissolved oxygen, and turbidity) averages; and (12) sensor installation methods. All files are .csv, .jpg, .jpeg, or .pdf.

measurementTechnique: Two sites, consisting of an unburned (W10) and burned (W20) location, were sampled approximately monthly from November 2020 until August 2022 to collect stream water chemistry data. Grab samples were taken for total suspended solids (TSS), dissolved organic carbon (NPOC), total dissolved nitrogen (TDN), and anions. Handheld sensors including a YSI, Ultrameter, and Manta were deployed during each visit to collectively measure dissolved oxygen, pH, specific conductivity, total dissolved solids, temperature, pressure, and turbidity. For more details, see YRBT_Sample_Protocol.csv and YRBT_Sensor_Protocol.csv.
